title.narrative: DRA Chad ACJR

description.narrative: Driven by persistent violence in Darfur, at least 737.679 Sudanese refugees (79%) and Chadian returnees (21%) have crossed the border into Chad since April 2023 (IOM, 2024). Over the last 4 months, population movements intensified, particularly in Wadi Fira (79.178 refugees) and Sila (92.611 refugees) provinces (UNHCR, April 2024). With new refugees arriving daily, public services are overwhelmed and competition for scarce natural resources increases, pushing vulnerable families further into poverty, hunger and malnutrition.With 442,112 children suffering from acute malnutrition, the refugee crisis has pushed the Eastern provinces into IPC 4. According to WFP, 468.000 displaced people will not have access to food in the lean season (June to August) if no food is provided soon. In Sila, food support is particularly needed with 15,927 people in IPC3 and 23.941 in IPC4 (cadre harmonisée, 2024), recognizing the sinking funds available to WFP.Last month, 45% of the refugees were relocated from spontaneous arrival sites, of which 19.348 to Mile camp in Wadi Fira and 3.156 to Kerfi camp in Sila (UNHCR 2024). According to UNHCR, WASH is among the most pressing needs in Mile extension camp. The nearest water supply is at >5 km distance, showing the need for safe water provision. Hygienic conditions are concerning as open defecation is common, increasing risks of communicable diseases. According to UNHCR, there is need for 620 latrines and showers as well as hygiene kits.Since 88% of the displaced people are women and children, there is a high need for protection services including prevention activities. 30,790 individuals including 19,090 children require psychosocial support, while 303.030 children are at risk of GBV (UNHCR, 2024).Therefore, WV and ADESOH propose an integrated multi-sectoral response in Mile extension camp and Kerfi camp and host communities around the camps. The project complements WV's ongoing interventions as well as CARE's protection activities in Mile camp.

The project prioritizes children, UASC, survivors of SGBV, women and girls at risk of SEAH and trafficking, PLW, elderly people and PWD. Sensitization meetings will be held to understand and comment on the targeting criteria, ensuring the response is contextual and transparent and inclusive. During distributions, UASC, elderly, PLW and PWD are served first to prevent a long waiting time. To avoid conflict and foster integration, the project will target 70% of refugees and returnees and 30% of the host population.

To provide essential WASH, FSL and protection services to 12.000 people in Wadi Fira (Mile extension camp, host community Kidirmon, Alarsamat and Bararingne) and Sila (refugee camp of Kerfi, host community Tondollo and Djangatiti)
